clue.text: Unseen and unenvied object has crazy upper class fool disappearing with cry of pain

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters before it go wild and come out in a new order
a fool disappearing from class means a word for a fool is taken out of it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ow is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: Something nobody sees or envies drives a posh idiot mad until he vanishes with a yelp.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ASS from CLASS leaves CL; 'crazy' turns UPPER plus CL into PURPLEC, and OW finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelett Burgess's nonsense verse says he never saw this creature and never hopes to see one, so it is unseen and unenvied.

clue.text: Leave with greeting by an archer leaving?

parts.note: to part is to leave or go away
hi is a casual greeting
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier departs saying hello beside a bowman on his way out.
explanation.walkthrough: A Parthian shot was an arrow fired backwards by a mounted archer while retreating, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Parthian horse archers famously shot while riding away, so one of them is an archer on the retreat.

clue.text: Additional comment being carried

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a document or statement as an extra remark
one who rides is carried by a horse or vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an appended clause to a verdict or bill, and a person carried on horseback or in a vehicle.

clue.text: Parallel point in floor covering for 24 — it's due for renewal

indicators.note: the point sits in the floor covering, placed inside it

parts.note: lino is short for linoleum, a floor covering
E is a compass point, east
24-across is RESIDENCE, and a flat is a home
the word it, its apostrophe-s acting as a link

indicators.note: renewal makes the letters of due new again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Floor tiling is being renewed for a house, with a point about something parallel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for renewal' rearranges only 'due'. The 24 points to the 24-across entry, a home, so FLAT is a synonym for that answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of latitude run parallel to the equator and are commonly called parallels, like the 38th.

clue.text: Photographer endlessly performing?

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a camera is the device that takes photographs, here standing for the photographer
on stage, a performer is on

explanation.surface: A photographer who never stops putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Julia Margaret Cameron was a Victorian portrait photographer; the clue reads as her description and as the instructions at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Julia Margaret Cameron was a pioneering Victorian photographer, so the surname names one.

clue.text: They shed light on computing frames

definitions.meaning: panes in a wall that let daylight into a room
the bordered panels on a computer screen, and Microsoft's operating system

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the glazed openings that let light in and the framed panels of a computer display.

clue.text: Strike-breaker and poet concealing weapon

parts.note: a scab is a worker who breaks a strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A blackleg and a versifier are hiding a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath for a sword hides the blade, so it is a thing concealing a weapon.

clue.text: Horsey gent caught having a good time with Love unfinished

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
having a ball means having a good time

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: Eros is the god of love

explanation.surface: A horseman is caught enjoying himself while his love affair is left hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish gentleman, originally a horseman or knight, so a horse-riding gentleman.

clue.text: Children's writer left in near heavyweight

indicators.note: the left goes in, placed inside the word for near

parts.note: by means near, as in close by
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: An author of children's books stands by a big fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton wrote the Famous Five and Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid Blyton is one of the best-selling British authors of books for children.

clue.text: Collector of poems etc sees right to work retained by our student?

indicators.note: retained means the collector holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: an anthologist collects poems and other pieces into a book
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An editor of verse collections finds the right to work kept by a student of ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our student' means a student of us, humankind, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies humankind, so is a student of us all.

clue.text: Sculptor with pickle?

parts.note: Chambers has 'a ... pickle' for a punishment kept ready, so the sculptor's name splits into that ...

explanation.surface: An artist who works in stone, accompanied by a gherkin.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a rod in pickle is an old phrase for keeping a punishment ready; the name splits as ROD IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker and The Kiss.

clue.text: All my life — and that's a lot — is about a Bond production

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: many means a lot

indicators.note: a production makes something new, so the letters of a Bond are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Bond film turns up repeatedly in someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's a lot' sounds like a comment but gives the word for numerous; 'is about' places it around the reworked 'a Bond'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic phrase for from childhood through adulthood, the whole of one's life.

clue.text: Shelter in shady spot after end of March

indicators.note: after puts the shady spot following the letter
end of picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: an arbour is a leafy shaded garden bower

explanation.surface: Seeking cover in a shady bower once March ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A port gives ships shelter, and the verb also means to shelter someone.

clue.text: Look both ways to circumvent the tragedy

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go around, so the backwards look surrounds the other word
both ways means look is written once backwards and once forwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
taken as written
lo again, the forwards way

explanation.surface: Glancing left and right to get round a sad play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' gives the old interjection for 'look' twice, first backwards then forwards; 'circumvent' wraps the backwards copy round 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about the jealous Moor is one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Not a chance for Mick with Kate then?

definitions.text: Not a chance for Mick with Kate then?

parts.words: Not a chance for Mick with Kate then?
parts.note: Mick Jagger is a member of the band whose name opens the proverb, and Kate Moss is the model, so the proverb denies him her

explanation.surface: A rock star has no hope of winning a supermodel.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a restless person accumulates nothing; read literally, a Stone never gets a Moss.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb, read with band member and model, says the singer never gets the supermodel.

clue.text: Device for managing, correcting or erasing

indicators.note: correcting puts the letters right by reordering them

explanation.surface: A tool for running things, used for fixing or deleting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correcting' works only on 'erasing'; 'or' stays as it is at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary or planner is a gadget or book for organising and managing one's affairs.

clue.text: Dangerous stuff preferably used during an emergency call

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: during means the word for preferably sits within the call

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
best means preferably, as in you had best go

explanation.surface: Hazardous material is ideally used when someone calls for help.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was used for fireproofing but its dust is a dangerous cause of lung disease.

clue.text: See 14
Ascetics found everywhere but the West?

parts.note: the letters are all compass points except W

explanation.surface: Hermits are found all over except in Western countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a world map; the letters are compass points, every one but W.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Jewish sect lived austerely in communities near the Dead Sea.

clue.text: Title on the side, which is enlightening

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the title above the other piece

parts.note: The Sun is a newspaper title
the beam is the side of a ship

explanation.surface: A title placed on the side, giving illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of sunlight brings light into a place, literally enlightening it.

clue.text: Capital of South Africa with tailless bird

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the bird is dropped

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A South African city linked to a bird without a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: Payment to pope or crown — either way girl has setback

indicators.note: either way means the name reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
set read back gives the letters

explanation.surface: A woman suffers a setback paying either the Pope or the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the first year's revenues of a church benefice, paid to the Pope and later to the English crown.

clue.text: Lighter dined with little stranger

parts.note: a neon is a lighting tube
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Someone with a lighter ate with a tiny stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little stranger' is an old jocular phrase for a newborn baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn infant is jokingly called a little stranger, newly arrived in the world.

clue.text: A horse, say, or other cause of trouble

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

indicators.note: other means the letters are made into another order

explanation.surface: A horse or something else causing a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGRO is British slang for aggressive behaviour or hassle.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for aggravation, hassle and hostile behaviour that makes trouble.

clue.text: Home for deer since dispersal

indicators.note: dispersal scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A place for deer to live since they scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a place where someone lives, a dwelling.

clue.text: Entered with precious lump?

parts.note: got in means entered, and read in inverted, poetic order it gives the bar

explanation.surface: Someone came in with a valuable chunk.
explanation.walkthrough: IN GOT is a poetic inversion of 'got in', meaning entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast bar of gold or silver is a lump of precious metal.

clue.text: See 6
All matter, including outback, is rich and splendid

parts.note: sum means the total, all

indicators.note: including means the matter holds the reversed word

parts.note: pus is matter from a wound
out read back, the second half of the word telling you to reverse the first

explanation.surface: All the stuff, the outback included, is lavish and magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outback' looks like the Australian bush, but it is OUT turned backwards; 'including' puts that inside PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumptuous describes something lavish and costly, rich and magnificent.
